solution: Cutting one head regrows a head, so move 1 is a no-op and the reachable moves are (H,T)->(H,T+1) for T>=1, (H,T)->(H-2,T) for H>=2 and (H,T)->(H+1,T-2) for T>=2. If a of the first, b of the second and c of the third are used then a = 2c - T and 2b = H + c, so the total 3c - T + (H+c)/2 is increasing in c and the optimum is the smallest c >= ceil(T/2) with c congruent to H mod 2. Such a plan is always orderable (all tail-growths first, then all tail-pairs, then all head-pairs), so with H, T >= 1 the answer is never -1. O(1) per test case, O(1) space.
statement_summary: A knight fights a creature with H heads and T tails and may cut one head, one tail, two heads or two tails, but cutting a single head regrows a head, cutting a single tail regrows two tails, and cutting two tails grows a head. The creature dies only when both counts reach zero at once; the task is the fewest cuts, with H and T each at most 100.
notes: The closed form was checked against a breadth-first search over the whole (heads, tails) state graph for every start with H, T in 1..100; they agree exactly, which is also why the bfs label is kept (searching the state graph is an equally valid solution at these limits). -1 is unreachable for the stated input range.
